description: Fix-forward cycle on the CAM-55 branch: the 10 committed stories pass gates but the new code never executed in the prior cycle (ran on the old supervisor). Staff review returned REQUEST CHANGES (FIXES_PENDING:4). officialDocsConsulted.summary: send-keys -l makes ALL trailing args literal incl Enter (no submit); for a submitting dispatch use send-keys text Enter WITHOUT -l, or split into send-keys -l text then send-keys Enter. set -p @user-option for per-pane labels.

userStories.title: Sidecar supervisor design doc (spike)
userStories.description: As the next implementer or operator, I need the PINNED sidecar-supervisor architecture documented so subsequent fix stories encode it without re-deciding: (a) cam run spawns runSupervisor as a DETACHED BACKGROUND SIDECAR process (child of the wrapper, not a tmux pane; logs to a file the dashboard can surface); (b) the sidecar is TRIGGER-DRIVEN via the .claude/cam-loop.local.md active flag (when active:true and the PRD has pending non-operator stories, the sidecar runs decideNextAction, respawns the titled worker-pane, polls scripts/cam/worker-report.json, repeats); (c) cam next is a thin-proxy that FLIPS active:true to trigger the sidecar (it may also narrate to the orchestrator, but does NOT ask the LLM orchestrator to dispatch workers); (d) the LLM orchestrator persona is the human interface and surfaces the sidecar's terminal report; the OTHER thin-proxies (plan/issue/ship) still inject natural-language requests into pane %0 via the FIXED send-keys.

FLOW.md explicitly rejects the 'orchestrator absorbs the loop' model (the rejected C2 architecture) and explains why (loses deterministic guards: no-progress streak CAM-36, dead-worker backoff CAM-44, MAX_ITERATIONS, supervisor lock, event log).

scripts/cam/patterns.md gains one durable bullet capturing the sidecar-supervisor invariant (cam run = sidecar host; sidecar = deterministic loop driver; orchestrator = human interface; cam next = trigger via active flag; worker-report.json = push completion).

userStories.title: Fix send-keys submit (fixes C1: thin-proxy + worker-exit-push actually submit)
userStories.description: As any thin-proxy (cam plan/next/issue/review/ship) or the worker-exit pusher, I need tmux send-keys to actually SUBMIT the line (a newline reaches the program) instead of silently injecting 'Enter' as literal text. Empirically: `tmux send-keys -l 'HELLO' Enter` yields pane text `HELLOEnter` with no newline submitted, because -l makes ALL trailing args literal including Enter. Fix: drop -l on the submit (working precedent: src/ui/Dashboard.tsx:190 and src/retry/tmux.ts:13 use `send-keys -t pane text Enter` with no -l), OR split into two calls (`send-keys -l text` then `send-keys Enter`).
acceptanceCriteria: src/tmux/dispatch.ts sendKeysWhenIdle's submit argv NO LONGER has '-l' immediately before 'Enter': either drop -l for the whole call, or split into two calls (send-keys -l text, then send-keys Enter).
src/supervisor/worker-report.ts (worker-exit one-line summary push) is fixed the same way.
.claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md (and any other agent doc that documents the send-keys form) is updated to reflect the corrected argv; the templates/ mirror is also updated.

An EMPIRICAL / integration test drives a real tmux pane through the helper and asserts the line was SUBMITTED (a newline reached the program), not merely that the argv shape is correct. Suggested approach: spawn a real tmux server in a unique socket, send a literal payload via the helper, capture-pane and assert the next prompt line is present (proving Enter was processed).
No unit-only-asserts-argv test is accepted as a substitute for the empirical check above (the bug we are fixing IS the argv-vs-runtime mismatch).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files: src/tmux/dispatch.ts (line ~189-193 the submit call), src/supervisor/worker-report.ts (worker-exit push), .claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md (and any other agent doc that documents the send-keys form), templates/.claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md mirror. Empirical test pattern: spawn tmux with a private socket via tmux -L <unique>, new-session -d, run a tiny `cat > /tmp/foo` in the pane, send payload via the helper, then read /tmp/foo to confirm a trailing newline (proving Enter was submitted). Clean up the tmux server with `tmux -L <unique> kill-server` in afterAll. Patterns.md invariants to re-check: send-keys submit has NO -l before Enter (this story is what creates that invariant; the existing patterns.md bullet that says '-l for literal payloads' must be updated to call out the Enter-arg pitfall); no em-dash in any persisted .md edit; Bun runtime (use Bun.spawnSync for the test tmux calls).

userStories.title: Fix .cam-orch-ready timing race (fixes C4: marker written by orchestrator, not by parent)
userStories.description: As a thin-proxy bootstrapping cam run, I need .claude/.cam-orch-ready to mean AGENT READY (not 'parent process is about to spawn'). Today src/commands/run.ts:281-285 writes the marker synchronously in the cam run parent BEFORE the orchestrator claude process is even spawned (respawn at ~line 308), so a thin-proxy sees 'ready' instantly and pushes send-keys into a pane where claude has not loaded.
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/run.ts NO LONGER writes .claude/.cam-orch-ready in the parent before the respawn-pane call.
The orchestrator boot prompt (buildOrchestratorBootPrompt) instructs the orchestrator to write .claude/.cam-orch-ready as its FIRST action after boot (i.e. the marker means the agent has loaded).
SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup in src/commands/run.ts removes the marker on parent exit (a crash must not leave a stale marker).

The thin-proxy bootstrap-wait helper (src/tmux/bootstrap-wait.ts or wherever US-006 placed it) re-validates orchestrator liveness via the orchestratorAlive predicate AFTER seeing the marker, before trusting it (defense-in-depth).
Unit tests cover: marker absent -> wait; marker present + orchestrator alive -> proceed; marker present + orchestrator dead -> fall through to bootstrap or fail with clear UX.
